Re: Public Records Act Request

Dear Alpine Community Planning Group Members,

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I am writing to request a copy of the records detailed below.

I am researching how the Alpine Community Planning Group (ACPG) conducts its business on the part of the residents of Alpine in preparation for publication of an expose. To that end, I request the following records:

1. All Alpine Community Planning Group Agendas and Minutes from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025.

2. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another member(s) of the Alpine Community Planning Group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

3. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and another government agency, including between the group members and the County of San Diego from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

4. All communications between any member of the Alpine Community Planning Group and any member of the public, including between the group members and individuals/entities with business before the group from 1 January 2024 through 31 May 2025. Please include current and former members during this time period.

Please note that the Public Records Act allows a member of the public to request records by describing their content, rather than asking for specific documents by name; an agency that receives such a request must “search for records based on criteria set forth in the search request.”

Public records represent “any handwriting, typewriting, printing, photostating, photographing, photocopying, transmitting by electronic mail or facsimile, and every other means of recording upon any tangible thing any form of communication or representation, including letters, words, pictures, sounds, or symbols, or combinations thereof, and any record thereby created, regardless of the manner in which the record has been stored.” (Government Code section 7920.545.)

1. This request applies to all records in your agency’s possession, including documents created by a member of another government agency or a member of the public.

2. If specific portions of any documents are exempt from disclosure, please provide the non-exempt portions.

3. Please provide entire documents, even if only parts of them are responsive to this request.

If you maintain records or data in electronic format, please provide them in that same format.

1 California First Amendment Coalition v. Superior Court, 67 Cal.App.4th 159, 165-66 (1998).
2 See California State University v. Superior Court, 90 Cal. App. 4th 810, 824-25 (1999).
3 Gov’t. Code § 6253(a). versions are acceptable) to avoid copying costs.
4 If you are unable to reproduce electronic records in electronic form, please provide a reason for doing so.

I request that you waive copying fees because I have limited resources, and the information requested will be used in the public interest to further the public’s understanding of the local community planning group action. None of the information obtained will be sold or distributed for profit. If you are unable to waive the copying fees, and you anticipate that these costs will exceed $50, or that the time needed to copy the records will delay their release, please contact me so that we can arrange to inspect the document or decide which documents we wish to have copied. Otherwise, please copy and send them as soon as possible. Please respond to this request within ten (10) days, either by providing all the requested records or by providing a written response setting forth the legal authority for withholding or redacting any document and stating when the documents will be made available.

If you require any clarification in identifying responsive documents or focusing this request, please contact [redacted]. Please send all records responsive to this request to Louis Russo.

Thank you for your time and attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

[redacted]

On Saturday, July 27, 2024, 9:00 AM, APG <associationofplanninggroups@gmail.com> wrote:

Good Morning APG Members,
Note: At the July 26, 2024 SANDAG Board of Directors meeting there was no (zero) County representation. This means we had no one representing the Unincorporated Area with the power to vote. Nora Vargas was absent. Joel Anderson was absent. The County Board of Supervisors has two alternates: Terra Lawson-Remer and Monica Montgomery Steppe. Neither were present. When a vote was taken to consider borrowing $20 million of future Transnet funds for the "Transnet Regional Bike Early Action Program" there was no one from the County to vote. We had an empty seat.
SANDAG's CEO, Mario Orso:
Mario Orso reported that SANDAG would continue to provide updates to the Board and stakeholders on the priority corridors of SR 78 and SR 67. He did not include SRs 76, 79 or 94 in this priority list. The Transnet Independent Taxpayer Oversight Committee is seeking community members for their Board. Information located at their website: https://www.sandag.org/meetings-and-events/transnet-independent-taxpayer-oversightSANDAG will not hold Board of Director meetings in August, but staff and working groups will continue with work.

APG comment to Board: This month we held the first Evacuation Tour with SANDAG and Caltrans staff. The potential evacuation routes in the Ramona area were thoroughly explored and wildfire hazards such as chimney fire burn zones were identified for the group by our local fire behavior expert, Dan Summers. The next Evacuation Tour will explore the SR 94 corridor from Campo to Jamul; including the dangerous intersection of Otay Lakes and Honey Springs Road. The Unincorporated Community values these opportunities to partner with SANDAG and Caltrans to share vital boots-on-the-ground knowledge in order to develop safe evacuation routes for all travelers in the region. Thank you.
California Transportation Commission (CTC):Two CTC Commissioners introduced themselves and reported that they are "the money people" for State and Federal transportation funds. Commissioners Clarissa Reyes Falcon and Lee Ann Eager invited Board members to attend an upcoming meeting being held in San Diego from August 15-16. Website for information: https://catc.ca.gov/meetings-events/commission-meetings-2024

Transnet Oversight Annual Report and Performance Audit and Budget:The overall feedback from the Board to those presenting on Transnet funds and projects was that there was a clear lack of information and accountability is needed. Cost Benefit Analysis was missing. Staff reported miniscule use of the public transportation options and utilization of biking or walking - Return On Investment is dismal. SANDAG often quotes the maxim that limited funds should be used to help the most people. Historically, the Transnet funds are benefitting very few. As of FY 2023, total bikeway Program funding was $397.3 million. Transnet funds represented $187.2 million (47%) of this spending. The promise of the Transnet funds to improve public safety through corridor projects is not being met. SANDAG staff's explanation was that the voters had an expectation and the funding sources for these projects (of which Transnet funds are only one part/source) come with stipulations that are often in conflict with what the voters expected. This is the difficult environment in which planning and funding for projects exists.
Melanie Burkholder, City of Carlsbad comment: We need cost benefit analysis for these Transnet dollar projects.
Mario Orso, SANDAG CEO comment: We are working toward structural change in order to provide cost benefit analysis and demonstrate a good use of the funds

Lesa Heebner, City of Solana Beach comment: I know that many people leave my city to move east because it is more affordable. This puts more people on those roads and they need to be improved.
APG Comment to Board: What are the raw numbers for this conclusion that bike ridership has increased 5x? Does this conclusion represent a change from 50 to 500 riders, 50 to 5,000? We need to see the numbers. And, do you see a slower increase in pedestrian travel than expected due to e-bike encounters on pathways?
SANDAG response (Omar Atayee): Those are great questions. We don't have those numbers, but will get those to the Board. We don't know if e-bikes are impacting our numbers, but we are seeing an increase. I don't know if we have data on that.
Dawn Vettes, SANDAG CFO comment: We acknowledge room for improvement and are working to strengthen internal controls. Our next audit in 2027 will show significant progress.

SANDAG's Youth Opportunity Pass:In response to a previous Board question about the cost per ride of those utilizing the Youth Opportunity Pass, Mario Orso reported .69 cents was the average cost.

emails.subject: Feasibility Study Interview Request - California State Water Resources Control Board
emails.body:
Good afternoon,

My name is Marissa, with Katz & Associates, and I'm part of a team under the California State Water Resources Control Board that is studying the feasibility of consolidating properties with individual groundwater wells or independent water systems east of Alpine with the Padre Dam Municipal Water District.

I'm reaching out today to see if you're interested in participating in an interview that will inform a Feasibility Study.

Background
The California State Water Resources Control Board<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/> (Board) under the Safe and Affordable Funding for Equity and Resilience (Safer) Drinking Water Program<https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/grants_loans/sustainable_water_solutions/safer.html>, is funding planning efforts, including a Feasibility Study (Study), to support communities and help ensure a safe and reliable water supply for the future.

Due to some water quality concerns of existing groundwater wells in the Willowside Terrace community, located just east of the city of Alpine, the Board is conducting a Study to determine if this community can be connected to the Padre Dam Municipal Water District<https://www.padredam.org/> (PDMWD) to ensure a high quality, reliable and sustainable water supply is available for the future.

The Study team is interested in forming an expanded study area to include additional properties near Willowside Terrace that also use an independent water system reliant on groundwater.

As the Alpine Community Planning Group, the Study team is interested in participating in an interview with you to gather insights into the communities east of Alpine, near the potential study area. The Study team is interested in a range of views, opinions and experiences about independent water systems, the services provided by PDMWD, and the possibility of consolidating independent water systems with the district

Please let me know if you are interested in participating in an interview and what your availability looks like for the next few weeks.

I look forward to hearing from you.

1400 Independence Ave.

Dear Chief Moore,
The public in the region of Loveland Reservoir in the Cleveland National Forest are in great need of your  long-standing resolution to public service. 

I am writing to follow up on our recent local non-profit Friends of Loveland Reservoir to Forest Service contact regarding Sunrise to Sunset access and the compatibility of the easement-protected "shoreline"  fishing program with Sweetwater Authority's water licenses and California environmental and water regulations. 

As you will see from this 4 year old email chain, this is something I was pleading for your help with and trying to help the Forest Service understand as far back as September 2020.

It is clear from the easement, land swap origination documents, and past  Forest Service oversight of Loveland Reservoir that volunteers are not a factor in the public's right and need to access the hiking, fishing, and birdwatching program.  I don't agree with the pursuit of such a program of volunteers, or with exposing Loveland recreation users to the risk of failure of it and another lengthy setback on therapeutic recreation and subsistence fishing for lower-income earners in the region.

Sweetwater is simply obligated by the land swap and easement to provide access to the lake until sunset 365 days a year. Supervision during those hours, or lack thereof, is Sweetwater's business, not that of citizens, or the US Forest Service.  This is all 100% legally unambiguous. Please call out your legal department’s claims otherwise and/or have that analysis reviewed by another independent agency.

Fortunately, others in the community are stepping up. Please create a path for remedies to having lost much of Loveland's public benefits since our earlier failed communications and failure to implement the protection and remedies at Loveland that so many of us have petitioned Supervisor Tangenberg to act on for so many years now. 

Sincerely,

Russell Walsh

Good morning Elise,

Great job yesterday! There was a lot of on-the-fly decisions and pivoting on the event, so huge kudos to you for navigating it all so smoothly. *	Consider allowing ~3-4 minutes to let folks join the meeting so they do not miss the intro also ensure to read the cover slide and welcome folks to “Deep Dive: XXX (bring in the title)” – help set the stage to the specific topic

*	I also think it would be good to say that “this meeting is being recorded and will be posted on our website for future viewing” (or something along those lines). I know zoom notifies participants, but it is still good to say it and verbally let folks know why.
